response.justification: Strong, broad senior engineer with genuine geospatial domain experience (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS) and proven low-latency systems work at Sociomantic/dunnhumby using D with async I/O, fibers and caching at millions of requests per second — both of which map conceptually onto routing data pipelines. However, the core hard requirement of modern C++ (or Rust) commercial experience is largely unmet: the only C/C++ professional exposure is roughly seven months at National Instruments over a decade ago on a C IDE, and the last five years have been almost entirely TypeScript/Node.js product and full-stack work. There is also no navigation guidance, map tiling, or routing-quality-assurance experience. Worth a screening call given the systems-programming aptitude, D/C++ adjacency and GIS interest, but only if the team is willing to accept a significant C++ ramp-up.
strengths: Genuine geospatial/GIS product experience and open-source map platform ownership
Proven low-latency, high-throughput distributed backend work in a systems language (D)
Senior/staff-level breadth, strong testing/TDD and CI-CD discipline, Linux and DevOps comfort
concerns: Minimal and dated modern C++ experience; no Rust at all
Recent years focused on TypeScript/Node full-stack, not systems or data pipelines
No navigation, routing, or map-tiling pipeline background; no explicit distributed-systems fault-tolerance depth

key_factors.factor: Low-latency systems and distributed backend track record
